verdict.description: The MODEL's own call; the engine recomputes the authoritative verdict from each finding's tier (see below). pass = meets goal + criteria; warn = meets goal with advisory issues; fail = a blocking finding exists.

score_vs_goal.description: 0-100. How well the artifact achieves the STATED GOAL in the GIVEN CONTEXT (not abstract/generic quality).

criteria.description: One entry per evaluation criterion supplied by the caller.

note.description: Evidence-backed reason it is or isn't met, IN CONTEXT.

findings.description: Detect with high recall, then classify each finding with the gate fields below. Empty array if none.

trigger.description: The SPECIFIC input/condition that triggers this problem. If purely theoretical with no concrete trigger, write 'none'.

reachable.description: Given the stated CONTEXT (input provenance/trust/scale/threat model), can the trigger actually occur HERE? Excluded-class concerns (DoS, algorithmic complexity, CPU/memory exhaustion, generic input validation) are 'no' unless you can name a concrete reachable trigger in this deployment.

applies_in_context.description: Does this matter for the artifact's STATED GOAL in the GIVEN CONTEXT (not in the abstract)?

blocks_goal.description: Does this actually prevent the artifact from achieving the stated goal / a criterion?

violates_invariant.description: true if the ONLY fix you can see would violate a stated INVARIANT/non-goal. If true, do NOT put that fix in `fix` — describe the tension instead.

tier.description: blocking ONLY if applies_in_context AND blocks_goal AND reachable!='no'. Everything else is advisory. (The engine re-derives this; set it honestly.)

evidence.description: Exact quote/line/loc proving the finding — no hand-waving.

fix.description: Specific, actionable remedy. ADVISORY. Empty string if none, or if any fix would violate a stated invariant.

summary.description: 2-4 sentences: does it meet the goal in context, and the single most important BLOCKING issue (if any).
